file.content:
OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept
            when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and
            brackets are stripped. The result must carry 8 to 15 digits after
            the '+'. It is then stored and returned in that E.164 form (e.g.
            '0412 345 678' becomes '+61412345678'). A value that cannot form
            valid E.164 is rejected with 400.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]+$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$'
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must
            be valid for the owner's city per the fixed region ranges
            (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099 for cities in the
            Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD table); a city with no
            known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. A malformed or
            out-of-range postcode is rejected with 400. It is stored and
            returned unchanged.
          type: string
          minLength: 4
          maxLength: 4
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            When omitted on create the server sets it to its current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The optional date of birth of the pet owner, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'
            format. When present it is used to derive the owner's 'ageBand'
            (computed against the registration date).
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even if another owner already
            belongs to the same household (same last name and postcode, and
            therefore the same household id); it only bypasses the household
            duplicate block and the owner is created as a declared household
            member (never flagged as a possible duplicate). Write-only; it is
            not persisted or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object

The baseline is preserved exactly: **2 tests run, same 1 pass / 1 fail split** as before my change.

- ✅ `functionalityStillAcceptsFlatAddress` — still **passes** (existing flat-address behavior preserved exactly).

## What I did

This is a preparation-only task. The named future methods (`normalizeAddressFields`, `Owner.getAddressLine1/setAddressLine1/…`) don't exist yet — they're what a *direct* implementation would create and overload. My job was to carve the seam where the structured-address logic will land, following this codebase's own idiom.

The controller already isolates every create-time concern into its own focused, Javadoc'd private helper (`rejectWhenDailyLimitReached`, `assignDerivedFields`, `rejectDisposableEmailDomain`, `toBusinessDay`, `customerCode`, …). Address normalization was the one address concern still inlined as a bare statement inside `normalizeOwnerFields`:

```java
owner.setAddress(addressNormalizer.normalize(owner.getAddress()));
```

I extracted it into a dedicated `normalizeAddressFields(Owner owner)` helper (matching the name the change will grow into), with Javadoc in the house style, and left `normalizeOwnerFields` calling it. Behavior is byte-for-byte identical — it's a straight method extraction.

**Why this is the natural and sufficient preparation:** when the structured-address logic arrives (normalize `addressLine1`/`addressLine2`, decide flat-vs-structured, compose the returned `address`), it now lands inside a focused helper instead of bloating the field-sequencing method `normalizeOwnerFields` — exactly the overload the task flagged.

I intentionally did **not** touch `updateOwner` or the `Owner` accessors: those "carry complexity" only once the new `addressLine1`/`addressLine2` fields exist, and adding those fields *is* the change itself. There's no behavior-preserving restructuring of the existing code available there without implementing the feature, so restructuring them now would be premature churn.
